summary: A quiet tape for the holdings. No held name has a print inside 5 trading days and none has a 4.01, 4.02, new 5.02 or large 1.01/2.01 filing in the 7-day window. The one new negative on a held name is DPZ: BNP Paribas initiated at Underperform with a $295 PT, a day after an EVP's ~$993K stock sale. KR's company-confirmed 12-03 call enters the 5-day window tomorrow (11-25). For new buys, the dated risks are ADSK (likely reports today, estimate only), UNFI (est. 12-01, 4 sessions out) and BLBD (company date 12-02, 5 sessions out). BBY reported this morning (8-K 2.02), so my 11-20 and 11-23 flags had the right date. On CVS a second Medicare Advantage proposal (Star Ratings reform) followed the 11-20 CMS audit rule, which deepens that thread. Per L2, I checked every name's own estimate and filings below. Holiday week: closed 11-26, half day 11-27.

Held. Raised from low. BNP Paribas initiated at Underperform with a $295 PT (11-24), a session after EVP Garrido's ~$993K sale (11-23). That makes two negative sentiment items in two sessions. Neither is an 8-K event, and neither touches a measurable thesis clause. The input has no price, so I can't say how far $295 is from the market. The 'new Group CMO Lara Thom, formerly of Guzman y Gomez' item reads as Domino's Pizza Enterprises (the Australian master franchisee), not DPZ (inference from the source and the hire), and it is not a 5.02. No filings. Next 2027-02-22 (file estimate).

Reported today: 8-K 2.02/9.01 filed 11-24 and the 'Reports Third Quarter Fiscal 2027' headline (enterprise revenue $10.236B). The 11-24 estimate was right. The event is done, but the input carries no guidance or margin detail, and BofA's 11-20 memory-cost margin warning is the open question. The market's reaction should come from the marks. The 'Balfour Beatty buyback' item is mis-tagged (BBY is Balfour Beatty's London ticker). Not known to be held.

The government has proposed Medicare Advantage Star Ratings reform (11-23; per the headline, UNH, HUM and CVS slid). This is a second federal proposal on MA economics in four sessions, after the 11-20 CMS-6098-P audit-recovery rule. Both are at the proposal stage, with no final rule or comment date in the input. WIC item is noise. Next 2027-02-09 (file estimate). Not known to be held.

DoorDash secured $3.29B of debt financing, $1.79B of it earmarked for the $65 Instacart deal (11-23). That lowers the financing side of break risk. The 11-17 DOJ review is still the open item, and no close date is in the input. Next 2027-02-11. Not known to be held.

My read remains a financing or contract tied to the FERC-approved Sabine Pass expansion, but that is an inference. The Overweight/$344 item is the one already logged 11-23. Next 2027-02-25. notable.headline: BNP Paribas Initiates Coverage of Domino's Pizza with Underperform Rating (11-24, $295 PT)
notable.read: This continues the 11-23 thread: the EVP and Chief Restaurant Officer sold ~$993K, and a day later a new bearish initiation arrives. That is the first sell-side negative on DPZ in my memory window. It is opinion, not an 8-K event, and it trips no stored clause, but two negative sentiment items in two sessions on a held name is worth the PM's eye. The CMO-appointment item from the same window is very likely the Australian franchisee (Domino's Pizza Enterprises), not DPZ, so I don't count it.

notable.headline: Best Buy Reports Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results (11-24; 8-K 2.02 filed 11-24)
notable.read: This closes my 11-20 and 11-23 high flags, and the file estimate was right this time, unlike BLBD's. The input gives revenue only ($10.236B), not guidance or margin, so BofA's memory-cost margin question is unanswered here. The marks should say how it was taken.

notable.headline: CVS Health Faces Potential Financial Impact from Proposed Medicare Advantage Star Ratings Reform (11-23)
notable.read: The thread escalates again: sell-side cuts (from 11-10), Warren's breakup call (11-18), the reimbursement report (11-18), the CMS-6098-P audit-recovery proposal (11-20) and now a Star Ratings reform proposal that hit UNH, HUM and CVS together. That is two formal federal proposals on Aetna's MA economics in four sessions. Leerink's 11-20 Buy is the only supportive item. Anyone proposing CVS is underwriting both rules.

notable.headline: DoorDash Secures $3.29 Billion in Debt Financing for Instacart Acquisition (11-23)
notable.read: The first deal-progress item since the 11-17 DOJ review. Committed financing removes one break path. Antitrust timing is still the dominant risk to the $65 spread.
